## The idea

Before any outcome is seen, simulate outcomes on the real covariates and treatment to judge **which estimands** (ATE, trimmed ATE, ATT, ATO) the design can deliver, and **with which estimator**. A prespecified order of estimands then picks the primary.

::: {.flow}
<div>Plan<br><span class="muted">estimands in order, tolerances, time zero</span></div>
<div>Lock<br><span class="muted">design data + plan, hashed</span></div>
<div>Assess design<br><span class="muted">overlap, balance, populations</span></div>
<div>Outcome-blind simulation<br><span class="muted">feasible estimands, estimator</span></div>
<div>Negative controls<br><span class="muted">GO / FLAG / STOP</span></div>
<div>Design report<br><span class="muted">reviewed and approved</span></div>
<div class="gate">outcome enters</div>
<div class="after">Unblind<br><span class="muted">checks hashes</span></div>
<div class="after">Estimate<br><span class="muted">the selected estimator</span></div>
:::

<p class="small muted">The lock is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: it makes later changes detectable and keeps the outcome out of the design stage. The simulation supports feasibility only over its declared family of outcome models.</p>

::: notes
One sentence: outcome-blind plasmode simulation has been used to choose an estimator for a fixed estimand; we use it to decide which estimands are deliverable at all, before outcomes, and then let a prespecified order choose the primary.
:::

## cleanTMLE 0.5.0

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Twelve functions, one per step**

- Plan and lock: `analysis_plan()`, `create_analysis_lock()`, `save_lock()`, `load_lock()`, `verify_lock()`
- Design stage: `assess_design()`, `simulate_design()`, `negative_control_ladder()`, `design_report()`, `export_design_log()`
- After approval: `unblind()`, `estimate_effect()`
:::
::: {}
**New in 0.5.0**

- Time zero and eligibility are part of the hashed plan
- A variable dictionary in the lock; it refuses covariates fixed after time zero or taken from the follow-up source
- An identification table in the design report: what was declared, with a response to each flag

**Status:** first public version; not yet tagged or released. Planned additions in `WISHLIST.md`.
:::
:::

::: notes
The 0.5.0 work was driven by the Rescue.Co timing problems: time zero is the transport decision, but the registry is filled in at hospital. The package cannot check timing claims; it makes them part of the hashed record before the outcome is read.
:::

## Simulation study: design and status

::: {.two}
::: {}
**What it will test**

1. The outcome-blind verdict grades estimability better than overlap diagnostics (share outside the band, largest weight, ESS, equipoise), even when they are tuned on the truth; agreement falls when the true outcome model lies outside the simulated family
2. Drawing new treatments from the propensity score grades correctly; keeping observed treatments does not
3. Choosing the estimand before outcomes keeps coverage; choosing by the smallest P value inflates type I error
4. Expected CI half-width predicts the realized one
:::
::: {}
**Where it stands**

- Pilot steps 1 and 2 done: calibration, five overlap levels, three true outcome models (inside, near, outside the family), n = 500 and 2,000
- Contrast pilot run and cached
- Decision rules fixed on 23 October, **before** its summary was read
- Next: read the summary (step 3a), size the full run, run it

<div class="keybox small">No simulation-study results yet, by design.</div>
:::
:::

::: notes
The rules, margins and comparators were written down before step 3a is run so they cannot be tuned to the results. A baseline-risk factor was added because overlap alone gives the verdict nothing a propensity-score summary cannot see; its fair comparator adds an events-per-covariate rule.
:::

## Rescue.Co: the re-execution

- Nairobi trauma registry; transport by Rescue.Co against other options; primary outcome GOSE 4 or below at six months
- Nine comparisons, each its own lock: L1 to L5 (L1 is the protocol's), sensitivity S1 to S4, and death within 180 days for the confirmatory comparison
- Two runs: the **first four months** (the protocol's check point) and the **final cohort**
- The outcome is withheld from the software; the analyst had seen outcomes in the parallel unblinded analysis, so this shows the rules can be applied without the outcome, not that they would have chosen the same without that knowledge

| | Done |
|---|---|
| Final cohort | L1 to L5, the 180-day lock, S1 to S4; registration bundle written 27 October |
| First four months | L3, L1 |

<p class="small muted">Every lock finished before the 1 November cut-off. Locks rebuilt with identical hashes on a second machine, an interrupted lock reproduced exactly with a different number of workers, and every lock in the bundle verifies against its hash.</p>

::: notes
The run went unattended on the desktop under a supervisor that resumes after interruptions. The confirmatory pick was made by the rule in the plan once L1 to L5 had design reports, and the final bundle confirmed it.
:::

| L4 | 3,739 | poor (30%) | ATT | ATT | <span class="no">0.40 SD shift</span> | FLAG |

<div class="keybox">The rule picked <b>L3</b>, Rescue.Co against other ambulance operators, as the confirmatory comparison: primary estimand the ATE. Its sensitivity versions (S1, S4) agree.</div>

::: notes
L1 at both points, L2, L4, S2 and S3 ran with main-terms TMLE only and no extension of repetitions, a compute decision made before they were built; L5 had both candidates without extension. L1 and S2 also shift a named covariate by more than 0.25 SD.
:::

## Finding 1: poor overlap and the fallback estimands

- Where overlap is poor (L1, L2, L4, L5, and S2 and S3 without walk-ins) the **ATE fails** bias or coverage; coverage falls as low as 0.29
- Estimands for the overlap population are often feasible, but they **describe other patients**: they drop a third to a half of the comparators, or shift age, injury severity, assault or injury at home by 0.31 to 0.44 SD
- The population gate rejects all of them, so only the comparison between ambulance operators can carry a claim

<div class="keybox">This is the paper's argument in one registry: whether an estimand is deliverable, and whether it is the question anyone asked, are separate checks.</div>

::: notes
The gate was declared before any lock was built: keep 80% of each arm and shift no named covariate by more than 0.25 SD.
:::

## Finding 2: at four months, no comparison could answer the question

**Between ambulance operators (L3, 226 patients): precision, not overlap**

- Overlap was ideal: **no patient** outside 0.05 to 0.95, and the super learner met the bias and coverage tolerances for **every** estimand on every simulated outcome model
- Every estimand still failed: the expected CI half-width was **0.12 to 0.15**, against the smallest important difference of 0.055

**The protocol's comparison (L1, 1,661 patients): both**

- **49%** of patients outside the band; every estimand failed the half-width tolerance (0.085 to 0.115) and also bias or coverage

<div class="keybox">The protocol's check at four months passed. The design stage says neither comparison could have answered the question at that point.</div>

::: notes
Wording for the paper: for L3, no estimand could be delivered with the precision the protocol required; it is a sample-size result, not a positivity result. Main-terms TMLE was badly undercovered at that size (coverage 0.53 to 0.57). For L1 at four months it is both: poor overlap and too few patients.
:::

## Finding 3: does the simulation decide differently from balance checks?

<div class="small">Largest |SMD| after weighting / simulation verdict. Balance passes when the SMD is at most 0.10. Highlighted: the two disagree.</div>

::: {.dense}
| Lock | ATE | Trimmed ATE | ATT | ATO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L3, first 4 months | 0.40 / no | 0.40 / no | 0.31 / no | 0.36 / no |
| L1, first 4 months | 0.47 / no | 0.36 / no | 0.18 / no | 0.18 / no |
| L3, final | <span class="dis">0.12 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.11 / yes</span> | 0.12 / no | <span class="dis">0.103 / yes</span> |
| S1 | <span class="dis">0.13 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.13 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.12 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.105 / yes</span> |
| S4 | <span class="dis">0.108 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.108 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.12 / yes</span> | <span class="dis">0.101 / yes</span> |
| L1 | 0.21 / no | <span class="dis">0.12 / yes</span> | 0.06 / yes | 0.07 / yes |
| L2 | 0.38 / no | 0.101 / no | <span class="dis">0.06 / no</span> | <span class="dis">0.05 / no</span> |
| L4 | 0.97 / no | 0.12 / no | 0.09 / yes | <span class="dis">0.07 / no</span> |
| S2 | 0.36 / no | <span class="dis">0.105 / yes</span> | 0.08 / yes | <span class="dis">0.06 / no</span> |
| L5 | 0.17 / no | <span class="dis">0.07 / no</span> | 0.06 / yes | <span class="dis">0.04 / no</span> |
| S3 | 0.108 / no | <span class="dis">0.08 / no</span> | 0.08 / yes | <span class="dis">0.05 / no</span> |
:::

- Agree on **23 of 44**; the simulation is stricter in 8 and more permissive in 13 (every one at an SMD of 0.101 to 0.130). The primary estimand would differ in **8 of 11** comparisons (4 of 11 at a 0.15 threshold)
- At 0.10, a balance rule finds nothing in L3 and **moves the confirmatory claim to L5** (any ambulance against other means), trimmed ATE; at 0.15 it keeps L3
- **Different is not better**: the case study has no truth

::: notes
Stricter: estimands that balance after weighting but which TMLE could not estimate within tolerance on the simulated outcome models; two of these eight rest on resolved cells, six on cells left unresolved by the no-extension decision. More permissive: TMLE within tolerance although weighting alone leaves an SMD just above 0.1; eleven of the thirteen are L3 and its sensitivity versions. L5's trimmed ATE is balanced (0.07) and passes the population gate; its negative controls were run on the ATT, not on the trimmed ATE. The simulation also gives what balance cannot: the estimator, the precision, and a verdict per outcome. Whether it is right more often is the simulation study's question, and its comparators are overlap diagnostics; balance after weighting could be added as a comparator before step 3a is read.
:::

## Finding 4: what to say carefully

**The estimator depends on the outcome.** Same patients, same propensity score: main-terms TMLE for disability (the super learner undercovered, 0.86 to 0.88); the super learner for death within 180 days (main terms missed the half-width).

**Several verdicts sit at a tolerance.** L3's ATT failed on half-width by 0.0001; the 180-day ATE passed at 0.0298 against 0.03; S4's ATE passed at coverage 0.903 against 0.90. The trimmed ATEs of L5 and S3 failed on one cell each, left unresolved; S3's would have passed the population gate. L3's decision rests on 12 cells unresolved at 300 repetitions.

**Negative controls read FLAG everywhere they were judged.** In the L3-sized cohorts no control can read inside the ±0.02 band, so GO is out of reach; in the larger ones some do, but one inconclusive control makes its domain inconclusive. None read outside, so no STOP. Urban household is 96.5% urban: almost no information.

::: notes
FLAG is not evidence of no residual confounding. A few intervals exclude zero but cross the band edge and read inconclusive, for example cooking with wood or charcoal in S3, 0.018 (0.004 to 0.033); the paper should not call them null.
:::
